reports.title: Ecopetrol Revises Timing for the Release of Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results and Earnings Conference Call
Table 1: Financial Summary of the Income Statement – Ecopetrol Group

desk.headline: Sales up 17.5% to COP35.1tn, beat; net income up 86% to COP4.8tn on high oil prices and record refining margins; no updated outlook

other.label: Production (incl. 100% of Brava)
other.change: -0.5% y/y; 728 mboed net of Brava minority

other.label: Integrated refining margin
other.change: quarterly record, vs $14.3/bbl a year ago

results: Sales rose 17.5% to COP35.1tn: Brent averaged $91 (+34%) and the crude-and-products basket sold at a premium of $19/bbl to Brent, the highest since 2015; a stronger peso and lower volumes held growth back.
Net income jumped 86% to COP4.8tn and EBITDA rose 29% to COP15.9tn, despite a tax rate of 37.7% (wealth tax and a 15% income-tax surcharge).
Refining was the standout: the integrated gross margin hit a record $45.6/bbl and Cartagena earned $55.8/bbl, even with major maintenance at Barrancabermeja.
Output was 747 mboed, flat only because Brava (Brazil) was consolidated from 18 August; Permian output fell 23%, and local gas sales dropped 22%.
The 51% Brava deal (about $1.1bn) lifted debt by COP14.6tn to COP119.5tn; gross debt/EBITDA is 2.1x versus a 2.5x ceiling.

guidance.summary: The results report we read gives no updated production, investment or profit outlook for 2026 or 2027. The new CEO set out priorities instead: capital discipline, more free cash flow, healthy debt levels and cost cuts.

points: First results under new CEO Joaquín Gutiérrez, who framed it as a new phase aimed at restoring market confidence.
He promised tighter capital allocation, stronger free cash flow to support growth and dividends, and a culture of cost restraint.
Operational focus is on growing reserves, reviving exploration and adding gas supply, including offshore projects such as Sirius.
He named geopolitical swings, higher logistics and financing costs and natural field decline as the main challenges.
call.source: CEO message in the results report (6-K Exhibit 99.1); no coverage of the 13 Nov call found

watch: Whether production holds up as Permian and Colombian gas decline, and how much Brava adds in a full quarter.
How long refining margins stay at record levels once Barrancabermeja maintenance ends.
Debt and the FEPC fuel-subsidy receivable (COP11.4tn, up COP3.5tn in the quarter) and any word on dividends.
